items.title: After her husband's death, Annie discovered he had placed 100 bets a day
items.description: Annie Ashton's husband took his own life after suffering from a gambling addiction. Since then, she's campaigned for stronger regulation of the gambling industry and greater awareness of gambling harm.

items.title: First north-west cloudband of 2026 to soak all states
items.description: The most widespread May rain in a decade is about to sweep across Australia as the first north-west cloudband of 2026 becomes a reality.

items.title: Wayne Swan slams 'view from Mar-a-Lago' as Labor faces another test
items.description: Labor and the Coalition are both acutely mindful of One Nation's rise and its determination to take a decisive role in a future conservative government.

items.title: PM says fuel supply now above pre-war levels, no word on extending excise cut
items.description: Australia's fuel supply is now greater than it was before the Iran war broke out in late February, the prime minister has said, while refusing to indicate whether the fuel excise cut will be extended.

items.title: Netanyahu's attempts to corral the UAE put Middle East politics on display
items.description: The question for the Gulf states is whether they are happy for Israel to be the dominant player in the Middle East.

items.title: The United States and China just made a pact
items.description: This week in Beijing, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping quietly admitted something the world has been slow to grasp: neither can afford a collision between their two countries.

items.title: Hantavirus-hit cruise ship Australians unlikely to be paid out, experts say
items.description: But the lawyer who led the class action in the COVID-19 era Ruby Princess case has warned the cruise company will likely argue Australian law had no jurisdiction over the matter.

items.title: The most difficult question faced by antisemitism royal commission
items.description: Jewish Australians told the royal commission that antisemitism has spread into everyday life. But whether the inquiry can handle what it has promised to confront remains to be seen.

items.title: Couple's warning after losing everything, including two dogs, in devastating fire
items.description: While Patrick and Susan Doyle escaped with their lives after the fire on South Australia's Limestone Coast, Mrs Doyle was badly burnt and their dogs, Mercy and Oscar, perished. They are warning others to be better prepared.

items.title: Jane Caro reckons Australia is kidding itself about private schools
items.description: "There are absolutely no statistics that say that because you sent your kid to a private school they're going to do better in life."

items.title: 'Grossly incompetent': Action taken against Latham after online outburst
items.description: Contempt proceedings have been launched against Mark Latham after he attacked a tribunal that found he unlawfully vilified and sexually harassed another state MP.

items.title: A Chinese undersea device found near Bali may be part of something much bigger
items.description: The discovery of a Chinese undersea monitoring device in a strategic waterway "shows the extent of both China's reach and its undersea ambitions" and has implications for Australia's defence strategy, say experts.

items.title: Neo-Nazis fundraising to challenge laws that listed them as hate group
items.description: The leader of Neo-Nazi group National Socialist Network, Thomas Sewell, has appeared in an interview online alongside notorious US Neo-Nazi James Mason, who is listed as a terrorist entity by the Canadian government.

items.title: Diphtheria is back in Australia. Here's what to know
items.description: Once a major cause of childhood deaths, diphtheria was largely eliminated through vaccination. Health authorities say falling immunity may now be helping the disease spread again.

items.title: A little box of joy came into my life at just the right time
items.description: This little box of joy is a microcosm, a mini-exemplar of what a small amount of local effort can do to help fix some of our damage of the natural world.

items.title: Nic Cage makes the leap to TV in Spider-Man spin off
items.description: Plus, Shaun Micallef dives into Australia's gambling problem and the Stranger Things creators back another sci-fi mystery.

items.title: ABC 50/50 quiz: Test your knowledge of patron saints, the Friends finale and a 90s club banger
items.description: Each question in the ABC 50/50 quiz has only two options: one is right, and the other is wrong. But there's a catch.

items.title: The secret life of flowers revealed in stunning photos
items.description: Have you ever looked at a flower up close?  Or wondered how plants are pollinated? Take a journey through the secret life of plants captured in stunning images by Australian botanists.

items.title: Amid grief, the NT's CLP rushes drastic child protection changes
items.description: Stakeholders have just one week to respond to sweeping changes to NT child protection laws that Aboriginal groups say could do "generations" of harm.

items.title: Israel targets Hamas leader, kills seven Palestinians
items.description: Seven Palestinians, including a child, have died in Friday's air strikes, which Israel said targeted Hamas militant leader Izz al-Din al-Haddad.

items.title: $40m bid for airline crackdown with warnings of fare rises, cancelled flights
items.description: The federal government has announced nearly $40 million to fund an overhaul of aviation consumer rights.

items.title: Judge declares another mistrial in Harvey Weinstein rape case
items.description: Harvey Weinstein's third trial in New York on a charge that he raped aspiring actress Jessica Mann has ended in a mistrial, after a jury failed to reach a unanimous verdict.

items.title: Video of 4m tiger shark beheading prompts call for change
items.description: A researcher speaks out against the fishing of sharks after footage of a huge tiger shark being caught and decapitated circulated on social media.

items.title: The southern Sydney bay residents say is becoming a mudflat
items.description: A bin that has been sticking out of the mud for 12 years has become a symbol for an ongoing issue of sediment build-up in Oyster Bay in Sydney's Sutherland Shire.

items.title: Israel, Lebanon agree to extend ceasefire despite new strikes
items.description: Israel and Lebanon have agreed to extend a ceasefire and hold new talks on a political settlement, even as Israel carried out new strikes it insists are not subject to the truce.
